name: node9
summary: Access control layer for AI coding agents that checks each tool call, blocks or holds risky actions for review, and records all actions.
use_cases: scan a repository's agent configuration on every pull request
score how exposed a machine is to a compromised agent
review past agent sessions on a machine
features: hold destructive git, SQL and shell for review
detect secrets and PII in tool arguments
wrap MCP servers and pin tool definitions

pitfalls.readme_said: Guard your agents: node9 checks every tool call via an agent hook
pitfalls.actually_needed: To test it without an agent, run the hidden hook handler `node9 check '<Claude PreToolUse JSON>'`. When it blocks, it exits 2, which is the Claude Code hook convention.

pitfalls.readme_said: wrap any MCP server (docs link only)
pitfalls.actually_needed: `node9 mcp-gateway --upstream "<server cmd>"` wraps a stdio server. It stays running after stdin closes, so a scripted run needs a timeout.

judge.observed: Check 1 blocks the SSH key read with exit 2 as expected, check 2 returns permissionDecision "ask" for the force push, and check 3 prints help including the posture scorecard line.

features.note: The gateway proxied the calls and printed 'Pinned 1 tool definition(s)', but it did not exit when stdin closed, so timeout killed it (exit 124). Because of that, the chained `node9 mcp pin list` never ran.

what_it_does.quote:
node9 sits between an agent and every tool it calls: files, commands, the network and every
app it reaches. Each call is allowed, blocked, or held for you.

who_it_is_for.quote: Works with **Claude Code · Codex CLI · Antigravity (agy) · GitHub Copilot CLI · Gemini CLI · Cursor · Windsurf · VSCode · Claude Desktop · Opencode · Pi · Hermes Agent · any MCP server**.

install_per_os.quote:
brew tap node9-ai/node9 && brew install node9   # macOS / Linux
npm install -g node9-ai                         # any platform
